title: SDK middleware: minimal carrier and resilient header bridge
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: We need a low-allocation, cross-language carrier and middleware that propagates minimal tracing + sampling hints across HTTP, websockets, and background workers. Current SDK hooks add variable allocations and fail when headers are absent or mutated by proxies (some customers rewrite long baggage headers). Goals: (1) Introduce a minimal carrier header format (compact fixed set) for critical fields: trace_id, span_id, sampled_hint, route_fingerprint. (2) Provide a resilient header bridge that synthesizes a carrier when upstream headers are missing or incompatible and that maps common vendor headers into our carrier. (3) Implement a lightweight middleware and SDK hook with <1 microsecond median impact on p99 hot-paths and no per-request heap allocations in common paths.
acceptance_criteria: SDK middleware implemented for Node/Python/Go with consistent behavior
Carrier header present as X-RD-CR (compact base64 payload) and documented schema
Fallback logic: synthesize trace/span when header absent, preserve upstream vendor headers into attributes
End-to-end integration test covering HTTP, websocket upgrade flow, and background worker handoff
Perf: median added latency <0.5us and 0 allocations in common path; CI perf benchmark included
Canary rollout plan: 2% traffic in us-west for 48h with automatic rollback on increased error rate or latency regressions
comments: 2026-03-02 - Maya Patel: Spike completed. Prototype (node/python) uses a 16-byte compact carrier (trace(8)|span(6)|flags(1)|version(1)) encoded as base64 in X-RD-CR. Early numbers show ~0.3us median overhead in local microbenchmarks. See design doc link.

2026-03-04 - Luca Rossi: Found a race under asyncio: contextvars copy when scheduling background task lost the synthesized carrier. Added task-local slot and lightweight copy-on-write path to preserve carrier without allocations.

2026-03-06 - Priya Narang (review): Please add mapping rules for common upstream headers (b3, traceparent, x-cloud-trace-context) and explicit tests asserting lossless roundtrip when proxy rewrites header case/ordering.
2026-03-08 - Luca Rossi: Implemented header bridge mapping and canonicalizer. Mapped traceparent -> X-RD-CR with priority rules. Added 14 unit tests for header permutations.

2026-03-10 - QA (Ben Cho): Integration test flake observed on WS upgrade path. Reproduced: headers dropped during Upgrade in our test harness behind nginx; fixed by copying X-RD-CR into the ws-subprotocol metadata during handshake.

2026-03-12 - Maya Patel: Opened SDK PR for Node/Python/Go (link in attachments). Next: add telemetry counters and tracing coverage to the console dashboards, then schedule canary rollout per acceptance criteria. Note: security asked for a short review about header content entropy — answered in design doc (no PII; trace ids are opaque).
